messages.author: 59e24b23b6b00e9d
messages.subject: eval=FALSE won't accept non-R syntax
parts:
Hi,
I'm trying to add to my document some chunks of code from a command line software whose syntax is different from R.
The default text highlighting in knitr is very clear and legible and so I place my foreign code into knitr chunks together with the option eval=FALSE (i.e. instead of using some LaTex verbatim environment).
Trouble is, it appears that R nevertheless checks fro the syntax and gives me errors if it finds the syntax illegal.
Error in parser(file, encoding = encoding):

Would be great to have some sort of a syntax.check=FALSE option to be able to include in the document codes from other languages for demonstration.

Thanks
Roey

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] eval=FALSE won't accept non-R syntax
parts:
You can use tidy=FALSE along with eval=FALSE so that the code is not
checked for validity.

The error message was only an attempt to validate your code; if it
fails, it will proceed anyway.

BTW, if you use other languages in knitr, you may want to define your
own engine so knitr can actually run foreign code:
http://yihui.name/knitr/demo/engines/

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] eval=FALSE won't accept non-R syntax
parts:
Oh, you must also have highlight=FALSE because if you have the
highlight package installed (apparently you do), knitr will use it to
highlight your R code, which involves with lexical analysis of the
code, and invalid code will cause errors.

Since v0.6.3, the highlight package has been removed as knitr's
dependency because it was broken on CRAN, but to maintain
compatibility with previous versions, knitr will silently look for
this package. However, I recommend you to remove.packages(c('parser',
'highlight')) if you do not use them in other places (and remember to
update.packages() after that).

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] eval=FALSE won't accept non-R syntax
parts:
If you remove the highlight package, knitr will still highlight your
code but with the alltt package, which is supposed to be in base
LaTeX. In theory knitr should add \usepackage{alltt} in your preamble
automatically, but there was a small bug which has been fixed now on
Github. You can either install the development version on Github, or
add \usepackage{alltt} manually in your LaTeX preamble.

Note I did not use the minted package because it depends on pygments,
which will be another hell of dependencies.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] eval=FALSE won't accept non-R syntax
parts:
The alltt package does not allow line wrapping, so I cannot do much
about it unless someone tells me a better LaTeX environment.

The highlight package is very sophisticated because the parser package
gives it very detailed information about every piece of the R code. My
simplified version is naive: it only tries to highlight function
names, comments and character strings. That said, you can always
install the highlight package if you want, and everything will come
back.

Regards,
Yihui
